hero.subtitle: Long R3 IGF-1 · Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I · 83-amino-acid IGF-1 analog
hero.copy: IGF-1 LR3, also known as Long R3 IGF-I or Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I, is an 83-amino-acid analog of human IGF-1. It contains a 13-residue N-terminal extension and an Arg substitution at position 3 of the mature IGF-1 domain. Published research has examined its IGF-binding-protein interactions, receptor activity, protein folding and experimental biological effects. Veracue presents the material strictly for laboratory research use.

research_snapshot.quick_answer: IGF-1 LR3 is an 83-amino-acid analog of human IGF-1. It carries a 13-residue N-terminal extension and an Arg substitution at position 3 of the mature IGF-1 domain. These changes markedly reduce its interaction with IGF-binding proteins. Published work on it comes from cell culture, animal models, protein folding and analytical chemistry. It is a research material, not an approved drug.

paragraphs: IGF-1 LR3 is an 83-amino-acid analog of human insulin-like growth factor-1. The name records its two engineered changes. “R3” marks the replacement of glutamate with arginine at position 3 of the mature IGF-1 sequence. “Long” marks a 13-residue extension at the N-terminus. The formal literature name, Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I, therefore carries the same information.

Francis and colleagues introduced the analog in 1992. Their paper set out to weigh IGF-binding-protein binding against receptor binding as drivers of biological potency. Their constructs joined IGF-I to an N-terminal segment from methionyl porcine growth hormone. They made versions with Gly or Arg at position 3. The authors also reported that the hydrophobic extension appeared to help the analogs fold correctly.

The foundational literature describes Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I as a recombinant IGF-I analog expressed in E. coli. That statement describes the historical research and says nothing about how any particular commercial material is made.

Native human IGF-1 has 70 residues. Mecasermin is the drug-product form of that native sequence, so it is a different molecular entity from IGF-1 LR3. Many suppliers list IGF-1 LR3 as a peptide, and this page follows that convention. At 83 residues with three disulfide bonds, however, it behaves more like a small protein.

molecular_identity.note: The IGF-I domain of Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I closely resembles IGF-I. The 2000 solution structure found the main differences at the N-terminus, where the first three residues of the IGF-I domain are substantially reoriented. The authors interpreted that change in terms of the analog's lower affinity for IGF-binding proteins.

why_researchers_study.intro: Researchers turn to IGF-1 LR3 for a handful of well-defined reasons. Each one corresponds to a body of published work with its own limits.

items.text: The analog pulls apart two questions that native IGF-1 tangles together: how much ligand binding proteins hold back, and how much reaches the receptor.
It activates the type I IGF receptor, so it serves as a tool for studying receptor-level responses.

items.h3: Insulin-receptor signaling in specific cell models
items.text: In some cell systems it also engages the insulin receptor, which makes assay design and interpretation important.
For example, bioprocess groups have examined it as a growth and survival factor in CHO and HEK293 cultures.
Its refolding behavior has also been studied as a model for how a disulfide-rich growth factor reaches its native fold.
Rat, pig and guinea-pig studies, for instance, show that outcomes depend on the species and the experimental design.

why_researchers_study.closing: None of these threads amounts to evidence of a benefit in people.

paragraphs: IGF-binding proteins (IGFBPs) circulate with IGF-1 and can hold it away from its receptor. In circulation and interstitial fluids, IGFs sit largely in complex with IGFBPs and come free only when proteases cleave the binding proteins. As a result, the amount of IGF-1 added to a system and the amount that acts can differ.

Foundational research found that Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I interacts with IGFBPs far less than native IGF-1 does, while it still activates its receptor. Protein-structure work also supports that picture. Its authors linked the N-terminal changes in the analog to its lower IGFBP affinity.

Reduced IGFBP binding is a property of the molecule, not a proven benefit. It changes how the analog behaves in a given system, and the effect does not run in one direction everywhere. In rats, for example, the analog's very low IGFBP affinity meant it cleared from the circulation faster than IGF-I did. In pigs, by contrast, an infusion of the analog lowered growth measures. Potency therefore depends on the biological context.
IGF-1 LR3 activates the type I IGF receptor, and that is the property the cell-culture literature relies on. Even so, it would be inaccurate to say the analog acts only through that receptor.

In HEK293 cells, LONG R3IGF-I, insulin and native IGF-1 each activated both the type I IGF receptor and the insulin receptor in a dose-dependent way. Notably, at lower concentrations, the analog produced greater activation of both receptors than either comparator did. Earlier work used H35 hepatoma cells, where IGFs signal through the insulin receptor. There, the Long analogs kept a similar potency relative to IGF-I as they showed in myoblast cells.
Receptor context matters, so a result from one assay or cell line describes that system only.

Native IGF-1 can refold into more than one disulfide arrangement. Milner and colleagues (Biotechnology and Bioengineering, 1999) compared in vitro refolding of IGF-I and Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I. IGF-I gave about 45% of the native structure and 24% of an alternative, mispaired structure, whereas the Long-[Arg3] analog gave about 85% and 10%.

The result explains part of the analog's appeal as a folding model. It also shows why analytical documentation should address folding, because a mispaired isomer has the same composition, and therefore the same intact mass, as the native protein.

Serum-free culture removes the growth factors that serum normally supplies, so cultures need a substitute. Insulin is the traditional one. Voorhamme and Yandell (Molecular Biotechnology, 2006) reported that LONG R3IGF-I supported growth and survival of Chinese hamster ovary cells in serum-free medium. It worked at concentrations far below those insulin required. In HEK293 cultures, it also acted as a more potent growth and survival factor than insulin or native IGF-1.

The response is not uniform. In a five-clone CHO study (Dahodwala and colleagues, Cytotechnology, 2012), one high-productivity clone grew significantly better with the analog. The other clones grew equally well or slightly better with insulin. In the original 1992 work, all three Long analogs were more potent than IGF-I in rat L6 myoblast cells. The endpoints were protein synthesis, DNA synthesis and inhibition of protein breakdown.

Each of these studies used defined experimental concentrations that belong to its own protocol, and this page does not reproduce them. The consistent lesson is methodological. Responses depend on the cell line and even the clone, so titration in the system under study is standard practice.
Rat, pig and guinea-pig studies show that the analog can be studied in vivo, although results depend heavily on species and design.

In rats, continuous infusion of the analog was generally more potent than IGF-I for body weight gain, visceral organ weights and feed-use efficiency. It was only about equipotent, however, for reversing carcass muscle loss in a dexamethasone-induced catabolic model (Tomas et al., 1996). In finisher pigs, meanwhile, a short infusion reduced average daily gain, food intake and plasma IGFBP-3, IGF-I and insulin, while plasma glucose was unaffected. In guinea pigs, infusion raised the relative weight of the adrenals, gut, kidneys and spleen (Conlon et al., 1995). Body weight gain and carcass composition did not change significantly, however.

These studies show why the molecule has drawn attention. They do not, however, describe human muscle growth, fat loss or any therapeutic effect. Their infusion and injection regimens are not reproduced here.

human_clinical_status.statement: No direct human clinical trial of standalone Long R3 IGF-1 was identified in the literature and trial-registry sources reviewed for this page. Human clinical evidence for native IGF-1 or mecasermin should not be transferred to IGF-1 LR3, because these are different molecular entities.
paragraphs: Trial-registry entries for IGF-1 describe studies of native recombinant human IGF-1 or of an IGF-1/IGFBP-3 complex. Those results therefore belong to different molecules. Analytical studies that measure the analog in human plasma samples are likewise assay-development work, not clinical evaluations of effect.

The anti-doping literature describes IGF-1 LR3 and related analogs as never approved for use in humans. This review is not proof of absence, because a wider or later search could find material that this one did not.

researcher_problem_solution.h2: Researcher Considerations When Evaluating IGF-1 LR3

sections.problem: Suppliers and search results often use “IGF-1” and “IGF-1 LR3” as if they were interchangeable.
sections.solution: They are not. Native IGF-1 has 70 residues. IGF-1 LR3 has 83, with an N-terminal extension and an Arg3 substitution, so check the sequence before comparing results.

sections.problem: Clinical information about mecasermin is sometimes attached to IGF-1 LR3 pages.
sections.solution: Mecasermin is recombinant native IGF-1 with its own FDA label. Its approval and label content therefore belong to that product and do not apply to IGF-1 LR3.

sections.problem: The letters in the name are easy to memorize and easy to misread.
sections.solution: “Long” is the 13-residue N-terminal extension, and “R3” is the Glu-to-Arg change at position 3. A listing that lacks either feature therefore describes a different molecule, such as R3-IGF-I.

sections.problem: Published masses for the same molecule differ by several daltons.
sections.solution: The gap reflects form. Calculated average mass is about 9,117.6 Da for the reduced chain. With three disulfide bonds it is about 9,111.5 Da, so a document should say which one it matched.

sections.problem: Lower IGFBP binding is often summarized as “higher potency.”
sections.solution: The relationship depends on the system. Reduced binding changes how much ligand is free and how quickly it clears, and the animal literature also shows outcomes that vary by species.

sections.problem: A growth or survival readout does not say which receptor produced it.
sections.solution: The analog activated both the IGF-1 and insulin receptors in HEK293 cells. Receptor-specific readouts and comparators therefore help assign the signal.

sections.problem: Cell-culture results with the analog do not transfer cleanly from one line to another.
sections.solution: Even five CHO clones from one parent line responded differently in a published study, so titration and clonal context belong in the methods.

sections.problem: It is tempting to carry an animal result across species.
sections.solution: Growth-inhibiting effects in pigs, organ-weight changes in guinea pigs and growth effects in rats show why the model species is part of any finding.

sections.problem: Searches for IGF-1 LR3 dosage usually come from people looking for a use protocol rather than from laboratories.
sections.solution: Published studies used defined experimental conditions that belong to their own protocols. Veracue offers no dosing, administration or reconstitution guidance because the material is Research Use Only.

sections.problem: Knowing the molecule is not the same as knowing what is in a vial.
sections.solution: The reference sequence and registry identifiers describe IGF-1 LR3 in general. Only lot-specific analytical documentation, however, describes a particular lot.

sections.problem: A single purity percentage is easy to over-read on a protein with three disulfide bonds.
sections.solution: Chromatographic purity does not show correct folding, and intact mass alone cannot separate disulfide isomers. Instead, look for the method, the mass form and some structural evidence.

sections.problem: Institutions need to know which category a material falls into before it enters a laboratory.
sections.solution: Keep the intended-use statement, receipt and storage records with the purchase file. FDA's substance registry identifies the molecule but does not imply review or approval.

items.question: What is IGF-1 LR3?
items.answer: IGF-1 LR3 is an 83-amino-acid analog of human IGF-1, also called Long R3 IGF-I or Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I. It has a 13-residue N-terminal extension and an Arg substitution at position 3 of the mature IGF-1 domain. Published research has studied its IGF-binding-protein interactions, receptor activity, folding and effects in cell and animal models. It is a research material, not an approved drug.

items.question: What does LR3 mean?
items.answer: “L” refers to “Long,” the 13-residue N-terminal extension, and “R3” refers to arginine replacing glutamate at position 3 of the mature IGF-1 sequence. Together, they distinguish Long-[Arg3]-IGF-I from native IGF-1 and from R3-IGF-I, which has the substitution but no extension.

items.question: What is the IGF-1 LR3 sequence, and how many amino acids does it have?
items.answer: IGF-1 LR3 has 83 amino acids. The reference sequence is MFPAMPLSSL FVNGPRTLCG AELVDALQFV CGDRGFYFNK PTGYGSSSRR APQTGIVDEC CFRSCDLRRL EMYCAPLKPA KSA. The first 13 residues, MFPAMPLSSLFVN, form the extension, and the arginine at position 3 of the IGF-1 domain sits in the segment GPR. Six cysteines form three disulfide bonds in the native fold.

items.question: How is IGF-1 LR3 different from native IGF-1?
items.answer: Native human IGF-1 has 70 residues. IGF-1 LR3 adds a 13-residue N-terminal extension and replaces Glu3 with Arg. These changes markedly reduce its interaction with IGF-binding proteins, while the analog still activates the IGF-1 receptor. Do not assume that findings for one molecule hold for the other.

items.question: How is IGF-1 LR3 different from mecasermin?
items.answer: Mecasermin is recombinant human IGF-1, identical in sequence to the endogenous 70-residue protein. It is an FDA-approved drug product with its own label. IGF-1 LR3 is an 83-residue analog with no such label, so the approval and adverse-event information for mecasermin do not apply to it.

items.question: What is the IGF-1 LR3 molecular weight?
items.answer: It is about 9.1 kDa. Calculated average mass is roughly 9,117.6 Da for the reduced chain and 9,111.5 Da with three disulfide bonds. Because the two figures describe different forms, both are calculated reference values, and neither is a measured result for a Veracue lot.

items.question: What has IGF-1 LR3 research studied?
items.answer: Published work has examined IGF-binding-protein interactions and IGF-1 receptor activity. It has also examined insulin-receptor activity in specific cell models, growth and survival in serum-free CHO and HEK293 culture, disulfide folding, and species-dependent effects in rats, pigs and guinea pigs. All of it is laboratory or animal research.

items.question: Are there human clinical trials of standalone IGF-1 LR3?
items.answer: No direct human clinical trial of standalone Long R3 IGF-1 was identified in the literature and trial-registry sources reviewed for this page. Human evidence for native IGF-1 or mecasermin involves different molecules, so it should not be transferred to IGF-1 LR3. This reflects the limits of the review and is not proof that no such research exists.

items.question: What are the evidence limitations of IGF-1 LR3 research, including safety?
items.answer: Most findings come from cell culture and animal models, and they vary by cell line, clone and species. Standalone IGF-1 LR3 has no FDA-approved human-product label establishing an adverse-effect profile, and the absence of a label is not evidence of safety. Findings on native IGF-1 or mecasermin should be kept separate because those molecules are different.

items.question: What should an IGF-1 LR3 COA contain?
items.answer: A useful certificate shows the lot number and the identity result against the reference sequence. It also gives an observed intact mass with the mass form stated, RP-HPLC purity with its method, and the formulation. Structural or folding evidence, the testing laboratory and date, and endotoxin where relevant complete the picture. Intact mass alone, however, does not prove correct disulfide pairing.

items.question: Is IGF-1 LR3 FDA approved?
items.answer: Veracue does not present IGF-1 LR3 as an FDA-approved drug. FDA's substance registry lists Long-(Arg3) insulin-like growth factor-I under UNII M9L22Y19H9 and CAS 143045-27-6. FDA states, however, that a UNII does not imply regulatory review or approval. Mecasermin is a different approved product.

items.question: Does Veracue provide IGF-1 LR3 dosing information?
items.answer: No. Published experimental studies used defined concentrations or exposure conditions. Those values belong to individual laboratory protocols, so they should not be read as instructions for a Veracue product. Veracue provides no human or animal dosing, administration or reconstitution guidance because the material is Research Use Only.

acceptedAnswer.text: IGF-1 LR3 has 83 amino acids. The reference sequence is MFPAMPLSSL FVNGPRTLCG AELVDALQFV CGDRGFYFNK PTGYGSSSRR APQTGIVDEC CFRSCDLRRL EMYCAPLKPA KSA. The first 13 residues, MFPAMPLSSLFVN, form the extension, and the arginine at position 3 of the IGF-1 domain sits in the segment GPR. Six cysteines form three disulfide bonds in the native fold.

mainEntity.name: How is IGF-1 LR3 different from native IGF-1?

acceptedAnswer.text: Native human IGF-1 has 70 residues. IGF-1 LR3 adds a 13-residue N-terminal extension and replaces Glu3 with Arg. These changes markedly reduce its interaction with IGF-binding proteins, while the analog still activates the IGF-1 receptor. Do not assume that findings for one molecule hold for the other.

mainEntity.name: How is IGF-1 LR3 different from mecasermin?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mecasermin is recombinant human IGF-1, identical in sequence to the endogenous 70-residue protein. It is an FDA-approved drug product with its own label. IGF-1 LR3 is an 83-residue analog with no such label, so the approval and adverse-event information for mecasermin do not apply to it.

mainEntity.name: What is the IGF-1 LR3 molecular weight?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is about 9.1 kDa. Calculated average mass is roughly 9,117.6 Da for the reduced chain and 9,111.5 Da with three disulfide bonds. Because the two figures describe different forms, both are calculated reference values, and neither is a measured result for a Veracue lot.

mainEntity.name: What has IGF-1 LR3 research studied?

acceptedAnswer.text: Published work has examined IGF-binding-protein interactions and IGF-1 receptor activity. It has also examined insulin-receptor activity in specific cell models, growth and survival in serum-free CHO and HEK293 culture, disulfide folding, and species-dependent effects in rats, pigs and guinea pigs. All of it is laboratory or animal research.

mainEntity.name: Are there human clinical trials of standalone IGF-1 LR3?

acceptedAnswer.text: No direct human clinical trial of standalone Long R3 IGF-1 was identified in the literature and trial-registry sources reviewed for this page. Human evidence for native IGF-1 or mecasermin involves different molecules, so it should not be transferred to IGF-1 LR3. This reflects the limits of the review and is not proof that no such research exists.

mainEntity.name: What are the evidence limitations of IGF-1 LR3 research, including safety?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most findings come from cell culture and animal models, and they vary by cell line, clone and species. Standalone IGF-1 LR3 has no FDA-approved human-product label establishing an adverse-effect profile, and the absence of a label is not evidence of safety. Findings on native IGF-1 or mecasermin should be kept separate because those molecules are different.

mainEntity.name: What should an IGF-1 LR3 COA contain?

acceptedAnswer.text: A useful certificate shows the lot number and the identity result against the reference sequence. It also gives an observed intact mass with the mass form stated, RP-HPLC purity with its method, and the formulation. Structural or folding evidence, the testing laboratory and date, and endotoxin where relevant complete the picture. Intact mass alone, however, does not prove correct disulfide pairing.

Veracue does not present IGF-1 LR3 as an FDA-approved drug. FDA's substance registry lists Long-(Arg3) insulin-like growth factor-I under UNII M9L22Y19H9 and CAS 143045-27-6. FDA states, however, that a UNII does not imply regulatory review or approval. Mecasermin is a different approved product.

mainEntity.name: Does Veracue provide IGF-1 LR3 dosing information?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Published experimental studies used defined concentrations or exposure conditions. Those values belong to individual laboratory protocols, so they should not be read as instructions for a Veracue product. Veracue provides no human or animal dosing, administration or reconstitution guidance because the material is Research Use Only.
